  content = '## Family is Everything

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is the MCU''s most emotionally raw film. While the first Guardians was a fun space romp, Vol. 2 digs deep into themes of family, fatherhood, and what it means to truly belong. James Gunn delivered a sequel that''s funnier, more colorful, and ultimately more moving than the original.

## The Legacy

- **Yondu''s Sacrifice** — "He may have been your father, but he wasn''t your daddy" — one of the MCU''s most emotional moments
- **Baby Groot** — Became a global merchandising phenomenon
- **Nebula''s Redemption Arc** — Karen Gillan''s character began her journey from villain to hero
- **Ego the Living Planet** — One of the MCU''s most unique and powerful villains
- **Awesome Mix Vol. 2** — Another chart-topping soundtrack

## Fun Facts

- Baby Groot''s dancing was motion-captured by James Gunn himself
- Kurt Russell''s de-aging for the opening scene was some of the most advanced digital work at the time
- The film has 5 post-credits scenes — the most of any MCU film at that point
- Sylvester Stallone has a cameo as Stakar Ogord, setting up the original Guardians team
- David Hasselhoff makes a cameo as himself, referenced in Peter''s childhood memories

## Viewing Context

Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is the **fifteenth MCU film** and the third entry in Phase 3. Set shortly after the first Guardians, it deepens the team''s relationships before they join the larger MCU in Infinity War.',
